problems.issue: Hallmarks are severely underreported: elevated desmosterol appears in 16% and corpus callosum agenesis in 23%, versus 100% each in R1-train. Developmental delay, ventriculomegaly and spasticity are also substantially suppressed, weakening the characteristic biochemical and neurological profile.

Example 3 combines gout and stage 5 chronic kidney disease with generic neurodevelopmental findings. These are not characteristic of desmosterolosis and, especially in this predominantly pediatric cohort, would teach misleading disease associations.

Example 2 includes mandibular aplasia and temporomandibular abnormalities alongside micrognathia-related disease features; this unusually severe craniofacial presentation needs justification and suggests excessive phenotype expansion.

summary: Sex and age distributions are plausible, and many simulated true features fit desmosterolosis. However, marked loss of reported hallmarks and unrelated severe findings make the simulated records clinically implausible overall.
